external_completion_check.name: Protected rule installation and an observed publication run
external_completion_check.reason: Zero protected rules are installed and no worker can install them. Their fingerprints derive from the family values of the two sanitization passes, which appear in no permitted input, and the scrub-publication environment holds no Actions secret. tools/scrub/provision.py can turn an owner-held private file of those values into the two secrets without printing, committing or putting one on a command line, but it needs the file. Until both secrets exist and the publication-scrub job is observed passing on protected main, GATE-SCRUB stays open and BOOT-003 is not done.

gate_validity.question: What does '0 protected rules' mean for a passing scan?
gate_validity.measured: A fixture repository was given a stand-in identifier in both a tracked file and a commit message. Development mode exited 0 and printed the same 'ok' line as on the clean fixture. The identical tree, scanned with a protected rule covering that value, exited 1 with two findings naming rule p2-001, source commit and source file, without echoing the value.
gate_validity.conclusion: A scan's coverage is exactly its installed rules. With zero protected rules the development scan is green over a tree that could contain any private identifier, so today's pass is evidence that the scanner works and not that the tree is scrubbed. This is now a checked property rather than a claim: tools/scrub/test_cli.py CoverageIsExactlyTheInstalledRulesTests runs the matched pair, and scan.py states the limit on every run that has no protected rules.

findings.detail: python3 plan/selftest.py exits 1 at this base with two failures: the legacy-identifier fingerprints in plan/check.py match nothing in docs/product-plan/reference/legacy-inventory.md, and compat/generated.rs generates no LEGACY_* spelling. Both were reproduced with this candidate fully withdrawn (the three modified files restored from HEAD and test_cli.py removed, then restored byte-identically), so they belong to HEAD, not to this work. Mechanism: plan/selftest.py's scratch() copies only plan/ plus work-breakdown.md, while the two vacuity guards R1-17 added to plan/check.py read files outside that copy, so the guards fire on the fixture. The failures are in plan/check.py, plan/selftest.py, docs/ and rust/ — all outside this item's lease, and plan/check.py is explicitly not editable by this worker. Worth its own item: those guards exist to stop exactly the class of vacuity this item measured, and right now they cannot be trusted to fire.

scan.py scans blobs, tracked path bytes and commit messages. An annotated tag's message is a tag object, skipped by the 'is it a blob' filter in historical_blobs and not covered by commit_messages. The contract scopes the scanner to tracked files and commit messages, so this is not a contract failure, but a public repository can leak through a tag message. Not fixed here: widening the scanner's object coverage is a scope change that should be contracted.

One of five full-tree runs exited 2 with 'configuration error: repository changed during the scrub scan'. scan.py samples HEAD, write-tree and every ref before and after a scan and refuses if any moved, which is correct fail-closed behaviour. In this worktree the refs are shared with nine sibling agent worktrees (refs/heads/worktree-wf_*), so a sibling branch moving mid-scan trips it. A CI checkout has no concurrent writer. Not fixed: relaxing the guard would weaken the exact-tree property it exists to hold.

notes: Re-measured at 606ff48c9b585e2ac5d801156c8a48a921d1b2b4. All six contract rows pass and are backed by an observed command; every rule added by this candidate was broken deliberately and observed to fail by name before being restored. No scanner rule was relaxed, no allow-list entry added, no test weakened or skipped. Marking this item done would close GATE-SCRUB and unblock the R10 publishing epic on a scan whose coverage of private identifiers is empty, which is the failure this repository exists to prevent.
